notes: Field, resolution, validation and documentation all shipped. Ran: fresh repo reports {source:default,value:all}; task override beats project beats built-in; illegal literal exits 2 at both set sinks; illegal stored value exits 1 at --record and --status; SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md and README.md document it.

Ran: under all a round whose only non-PASS row is severity info records clean=false, findings=1. AuditRowsClean returns false for any non-PASS row when convergeOn != blocking.

Ran under blocking: info and warning record clean=true; error records clean=false; severity "bogus", null, absent, 3 (non-string), "WARNING" and " info " all record clean=false. Fail-closed by exclusion (advisory set names warning/info only).

Ran on --record and --status: a clean-but-not-converged blocking round with one accepted row yields "1 accepted row carried forward — run the next audit round: ...", textually different from the empty round's "run the next audit round: ...".

Ran on --record and --status: a converged blocking round holding two non-PASS rows yields "converged over 2 accepted rows — implementation verified, proceed to release"; an all-PASS converged round yields the bare string. tp resume on the same fixture reports phase: release.

Replay of the committed 9-round v0.35.0 projection gives blocking 3 / all 9 at audit_clean_rounds 2 and 2 / 8 at 1. Ran both named mutants in a repo copy: grading error advisory moved 3->2 and 2->1 and no all cell; inverting the comparator swapped the columns. Both killed the test.

Row 3. Row 4, both halves asserted separately. Row 8. Ran all four shapes end-to-end under blocking — severity "bogus", null, absent key, and the number 3 — every one records clean=false. Row 9. Ran: recorded an info-only round under all (clean=false), then set --project blocking without re-recording; tp audit --status still reports audit_rounds[0].clean=false and consecutive_clean=0. The reporting path reads rounds[n-1].Clean from the store and never re-grades.

Row 9b, the relaxing direction. Ran: recorded an info-only round under blocking (clean=true), then set the project value back to all; tp audit --status still reports clean=true and consecutive_clean=1. No read-side floor re-blocks it.

Row 10. Ran on both sinks with audit_clean_rounds=1 and blocking: --record and --status both emit "converged over 2 accepted rows — implementation verified, proceed to release", and an all-PASS converged round emits the bare string on both. The numeral is what makes them textually different.

Row 10b. Ran the default arm: a clean-but-not-converged blocking round emits "1 accepted row carried forward — run the next audit round: ..." on --record and the same on --status; the empty round emits the unprefixed string. The count reaches both arms, not only the converged one.

Row 12's three simple assertions all hold (ran: exit 2 at tp set --workflow, at its --project form, and at tp import). But a --project write that changes the resolved value for a base OTHER than the discovered task file exits 0: with a.tasks.json holding task-level all and b.md holding no override, the unattended project write of blocking succeeded and b moved default->project blocking. fenceAuditConvergeOnSet resolves one base, not every base.

Row 13, all three must-pass writes ran green under TP_UNATTENDED=1: any write of all (task and project sinks); a --project write of blocking beneath a task override of all (exit 0, resolved stays all); and an import carrying an already-resolved blocking forward (exit 0). A field- or value-scoped fence would refuse the third.

Row 13b ran exactly as written: into a zero-task shell with task-level all and project-level blocking, a document carrying "workflow":{"review_max_rounds":5} and naming neither literal exits 2 at the fence. The precondition also ran: re-importing over a tasks-bearing target exits 3 at the exists-guard, so a weaker fixture would pass green.

Row 13d ran: over the same zero-task shell under TP_UNATTENDED=1, a document omitting the top-level workflow key imports cleanly (and the task-level all is carried forward — resolved stays override/all), and a document carrying "audit_converge_on":"all" imports cleanly. The fence compares tf.Workflow after the preservation step, which is what makes the first pass.

Row 16 ran: tp audit --merge --json --compact still carries by_severity with the same four buckets, while overlap_report is stripped. It is written into the summary map outside the !IsCompact() guard.
